thread.title: Dow Jones Loss Hits 1,400 Points; 4 Market Bottom Keys | Investor's Business Daily

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Dow Jones Loss Hits 1,400 Points; 4 Market Bottom Keys | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Virtually every stripe and color of stocks today slid hard following a rigid stance by the Federal Reserve to continue raising the cost of money, and institutions pounded Wall Street with heavy sell orders. The Dow Jones industrial average, at one point falling nearly 700 points, stretched its weekly loss to more than 1,400 points.
At around 3 p.m. ET, the Dow shaved its daily loss to around 1.8%.
The Nasdaq composite performed worse, at one point sinking nearly 2.9% before cutting that loss to around 1.3% with less than an hour to go on Wall Street's regular session. At its session low of 6484, the tech-heavy index fell more than 20% below an all-time high of 8133.30.
This marked the first time that the leading index for U.S. growth equities hit a "bear market" correction for the first time since 2011.
Over the course of an eight-month roller coaster ride from July 2015 to February 2016, the Nasdaq composite had fallen 19.5% (from a 5231 peak to a 4209 valley) before resuming its mega-trend bull run.
Defensive Sectors Rally Investors are reacting to the growing possibility of a slowdown in corporate earnings growth and the huge slide in crude oil prices. While lower gasoline and petroleum costs benefit consumers and certain industries, it also threatens the jobs of workers in the oil exploration and production markets.
A handful of names within the IBD 197 industry groups bucked the downward trend: gold and silver mining stocks rose more than 4% as a group. Meat, newspaper, auto and truck parts and water utility shares also advanced.
Kirkland Lake Gold ( KL ), which has earned a spot in recent months in the IBD 50 , rallied more than 3% to 24.88. The highly profitable gold mine operator remains barely in the 5% buy zone following a solid breakout past a 23.96 proper buy point in a cup base. If the stock were to fall more than 7% below the 23.96 entry point, it would trigger the golden rule of investing in growth stocks.
Please read this Stock Spotlight column on Kirkland Lake Gold to learn more about the Toronto-based company's fundamentals and an analysis of its stock chart action.
According to IBD Stock Checkup , Kirkland now snags a top-notch 99 Composite Rating on a scale of 1 to 99. This means the stock's fundamental, technical and institutional fund sponsorship criteria are at superior levels relative to both the entire IBD stock database and vs. its industry peers.
The S&P 500 dove nearly 1.3%. At the session low of 2450, the large cap benchmark has now fallen nearly 17% below its all-time peak of 2940.
Dow Jones Component Apple Still Stumbles Apple ( AAPL ), still one of the largest companies on the U.S. exchanges, continues to grope for a short-term bottom. The iPhone, MacBook and digital services giant briefly hit a multimonth low of 155.30 before rebounding some and cutting the loss to less than 2%. At the session's low, Apple's gain from a first-stage breakout from a cup with handle at 118.12 on Jan. 6, 2017, shrank to 31%.
FANG stock Netflix ( NFLX ) shaved its loss from around 5% to around 2% as the video streaming pioneer tries to hold above the psychologically key 250 level. Alphabet ( GOOGL ) also cut its losses amid a third test of institutional support near the 1,000 price level.
Netflix shares have slumped nearly 41% below a 423.20 peak.
The Dow Jones utility average traded nearly flat. Duke Energy ( DUK ) of Charlotte, N.C., featured in IBD's The Income Investor, is trying to halt a four-day selling streak. Shares in the large-cap diversified utility rallied nearly 1% to 88.06.
Watch for potential institutional buying support at the 10-week moving average, drawn in red on every IBD stock chart and in MarketSmith .
When Will The Dow Jones And Other Indexes Hit Bottom? At this point, growth stock investors can time their next entry into the inevitable new market uptrend by watching the Nasdaq and S&P 500 on a day-to-day basis and identify a follow-through rally .
This special up day, appearing usually on Day 4 or later in a new rally attempt, does not always work. It does produce fake-out rallies. But IBD research has found that every major market bottom since 1900 featured the follow-through .
Three more elements to watch for:
One: Watch for a dry-up in the number of companies hitting 52-week or all-time lows. On Thursday, at least 2,500 stocks did so. In a healthy stock market, new highs typically exceed new lows.
Two: Eye a major sector rotation. Right now, defensive sectors such as Food and Beverage, Media, Telecom and Utility crowd the top of IBD's stock research tables . These tables separate each stock into one of 33 broad industry sectors. Leading stocks tend to hail from the top five or six sectors.
Three: Look for positive price-and-volume action among companies that make IBD's top stock lists.
They include IBD Big Cap 20 , IBD 50 , Sector Leaders and IPO Leaders . When stocks with excellent EPS ratings and significant SMR grades (Sales + Margins + Return on equity) stop falling in heavy volume and begin to rise in stronger turnover, you are getting a direct message from institutional-class investors that they are regaining a strong appetite for U.S. equities.
Palo Alto Networks Is Rebounding Some Currently within the Big Cap 20, No. 1-ranked Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) edged up around 0.3% to 179.45 in above-average volume, gaining ground for a third straight session.
Watch to see if the enterprise-class security software expert can clear upside resistance at its falling 50-day moving average, currently near 183. Palo Alto trades 25% below a 52-week high and is still in the early stages of building a new base.
Notice, too, on an IBD daily chart how the stock's relative strength line has been rising sharply for four weeks in a row, a bullish sign.
In Other Financial Markets: Government bonds continued to gain demand. The yield on the benchmark U.S. Treasury 10-year note held firm at 2.77%. That's still up from 2.46% at the beginning of 2018.
WTI crude oil futures got slammed again. Near-term futures fell more than 4% and briefly breached the $46 level per barrel. At the session low of $45.67, West Texas Intermediate oil prices have now fallen more than 40% below this year's peak near $76.90 and touched levels not seen since September 2017.
Gold jumped 0.8% to $1,266 a troy ounce. Platinum gained more than 1% while silver eked out a tiny gain.
